Break the meta description paragraph into two: one paragraph quoting and contrasting the meta descriptions (under 60 words), and a separate paragraph for the page title change (under 60 words). Each should state its finding in the first sentence.
Add a one-sentence plain-language gloss immediately after the first appearance of 'multimodal revenue signal processing' — e.g. 'processing signals from calls, emails, and CRM data simultaneously'.

Split the third H3 paragraph into two: first paragraph covers the section-heading contrast (finding + explanation), second paragraph covers the buyer-profile implication (CRO/RevOps vs VP of Sales). Each paragraph should open with its finding.

Rewrite the opening of the first H3 block to lead with the most interesting finding — the paradox that Gong dropped its own category name after years of building that category — rather than a plain Before/After template.

Add a dedicated sentence or short paragraph explaining the 'OS' (operating system) framing in the page title section — this is identified in evidence as the strategic linchpin and the draft undersells it.
riskFlags: The claim 'That shift is consistent with a page that no longer needs to explain what Gong does' is an inference not directly traceable to evidence — it should be hedged with 'may suggest' or 'is consistent with the interpretation that'.

The statement 'your messaging may still be written for a buyer your product has moved past' in the founder test implies a causal outcome without a condition — needs a condition clause, e.g. 'if your ICP has shifted but your homepage copy has not'.

Quoting 'multimodal revenue signal processing' and 'specialized AI agents' from the meta description without flagging that these are Gong's own marketing claims (not independently verified capabilities) could mislead readers about product reality.

The phrase 'Revenue AI OS' appears in bold quotes in context, which is positive for semantic relevance to searchers studying the Gong repositioning.

The founder test at the end creates dwell-time engagement but is not formatted in a way that Google's featured snippet algorithm can easily extract — consider a short bulleted action list for the test.
